Cost of Furniture Cleaning – 2026 Latest Update

October 17, 2024
Table of Contents

If you want to do some furniture cleaningaround your house, one of the first things you need to learn is the cost of furniture cleaning. It can add up quickly if you’re not prepared. Learning the professional furniture cleaning costwill help you be a smart shopper and get a quality service at a reasonable price.

The national average furniture cleaning costcan range from $84, up to about $523. While it is nice to know these ranges of furniture cleaning prices, they might not tell you enough to get an accurate idea of how much it will cost to have your furniture cleaned.

That’s why we’re breaking down the latest on what to budget in 2024 for top-to-bottom furniture cleaning. Read on for clear details before requesting quotes so you know reasonable rates to expect from providers in your area this year. We have used the knowledge of our expert cleaning team to tell you all about the furniture cleaning service costyou can expect to pay.

How Much Does It Cost To Have Furniture Professionally Cleaned?

When you are having your furniture professionally cleaned, the price you pay will depend upon the type of fabric it is made of and how big it is. The average price people pay for professional furniture cleaning is about $173.

You can imagine that your furniture cleaning cost will depend upon the area you live and the prices people are willing to pay there, same in basement remodeling cost. In a high cost of living area, you can expect to pay for furniture cleaning, while in a low cost of living place you will most likely pay less for furniture cleaning.

In a high cost of living area you pay more because wages need to be higher so that people working as furniture cleaners can afford to live. You might also consider the number of furniture cleaners in your area, because if there is more competition, the price should be lower.

Furniture Cleaning Cost Factors

When it comes to furniture cleaning costs, a few key things affect what you’ll pay to get your sofa, chairs, and tables looking refreshed. Let’s break it down:

Furniture Cleaning By Furniture Type

The type of furniture that you need to clean will have a fairly large impact on the price that you will pay for professional furniture cleaning. For the most part, the bigger the furniture, the higher the price will be because it takes more time to clean a larger piece of furniture than a small one.

For example, while a dining chair with upholstery on it might only cost $15 for cleaning, a large sectional couch could cost as much as $225. This is a pretty big difference because the more fabric a piece of furniture has, the more upholstery cleaningproducts the cleaner will need to use.

You probably understand that the size of your furniture will determine what you end up paying. Here is a breakdown of the type of furniture and the range of prices a professional cleanerswill likely charge for them:

  • Couch or Sofa = $100 to $300
  • Loveseat = $60 to $120
  • Recliner = $60 to $80
  • Ottoman = $29 to $50

Material Of Furniture And Its Price

Different types of materials or upholstery that make up your furniture will have an impact on the cleaning process, and therefore the price. Some materials are relatively easy to clean, while some require special care or even special machinery to clean properly without damage, from this the prices are not the same in upholstery cleaning prices.

You can read the label on your furniture to see what type of cleaning it requires to give you a better idea of how much it will end up costing.

  • If you see a “W” on your furniture label, it is safe to clean it with water, and the cleaning method should be easier and less expensive, but not always.
  • If you see an “S” on your furniture label, it needs to be cleaned with a solvent based cleaner, which could require more special treatment and more cost.
  • If your furniture label has an “S/W” on it, it is safe to clean with either water or a solvent and it could be cheaper to clean it, or more expensive.

More delicate furniture, like those made of suede or wool, could be very expensive to clean because they will require a lot of care. Furniture made from polyester, or even cotton could be less expensive because these materials can often stand up to different cleaning methods.

Furniture Condition

Are your couches totally trashed by the kids? Or just need a quick pick-me-up? If your furniture is old or worn out from heavy use, it will likely cost more to clean. Newer, gently used furniture won’t need as much work.

Cleaning Method

Going beyond regular vacuuming and dusting bumps up costs, especially if commercial carpet cleaner rental machines get hauled out. Deep cleaning methods like using steam cleaners cost more. Fancy wood furniture might need special cleaners that cost extra.

Stain Removal

Expect to pay more if you need tough stains addressed. Set-in grease, mud, food, beverages, or pet stains can take serious elbow grease costing $25+ per stain. Be upfront so techs use the right removers from the start instead of making return trips.

Protective Treatments

Applying a protective coating to your furnishings guards against future stains and damage. Although an added expense upfront, treatments can save money over time by avoiding costly repairs or replacements later.

Common Furniture Protectants:

  • Waterproofing spray for outdoor sets (~$15)
  • Stain guarding cushions ($20 per piece)
  • Fabric protection like Scotchgard (~$15 per cushion)

Retreat every 6-12 months for optimal protection

Repairs

Before cleaning crew arrives, know if your furniture needs actual repairs. Wobbly chairs, missing hardware, pet scratches, or re-stretching saggy upholstery averages $70 per item. You’ll pay separate basic cleaning fees too. Prioritize what’s absolutely necessary.

Sanitization

Especially for recent second-hand finds, sanitization kills germs and bacteria. Steaming, UV light, or other methods start around $30 per seat adding to basic cleaning fees. Only spend if true sanitation is a must – simple soap and water do wonders for most used sets!

Labor

The amount of human effort involved makes up a significant portion of quotes from cleaning providers. Hand detail cleaning takes skill and time – factors that translate into higher hourly rates.

Labor Cost Considerations:

  • Number of technicians: Expect fees based on $35+ per hour per cleaner. Jobs may require a team effort depending on the size of the furniture.
  • Size of furniture pieces: Larger sectionals, wraparound sofas with multiple cushions, or expansive dining sets naturally take more scrubbing and will upcharge service rates.

The condition and size of your furnishings as well as the desired cleaning intensity all contribute to the hands-on time invested. Maintain transparency with expectations when consulting quotes so there are no surprise upticks in labor fees later. Technician time is generally the biggest line item.

Is Furniture Cleaning Worth It?

If you want your furniture to last for as long as possible, furniture cleaning is the only way you will have your beloved items in your home for a long time. Furniture cleaning is much cheaper than new furniture, but when you do it regularly, your furniture will look and feel like new for a long time plus you can save with your cleaning services prices.

Cleaning your furniture often helps the fabric stay strong, beautiful and smelling good. When you neglect to have your furniture professionally cleaned, dirt, grime, and oils make their way deep into the fabric and cause all sorts of problems that may not be fixable.

Furniture that gets thrown away because it wasn’t professionally cleaned will end up taking up a huge amount of space in a landfill. Just like when painting kitchen cabinet, always hire professionals to avoid mistakes or redoing it. When you have your furniture cleaning done by experts, you are doing a good service to the environment by keeping trash out of landfills plus they also .

5 Tips To Save Money On Furniture Cleaning

Yes, there are many opportunities to make your furniture cleaning even cheaper. Consider these suggestions to work within your price range:

1. Do prep work yourself first

Tackle basic vacuuming, dusting, and decluttering before the pros arrive. Thorough pre-treatment cuts billable hours for basic service fees.

2. Evaluate the cleaning levels needed

Assess if deep chemical cleaning, sanitization, or stain removal beyond surface wiping is necessary. Optimize quotes for non-intensive methods often adequate for gentle family use.

3. Ask about product bundles

Inquiring about package deals on protectants paired with cleaning services may offer bundled discounts. Some firms offer loyalty memberships with regular service rewards as well.

4. Consider DIY for non-delicates

Trust your elbow grease for hardwearing items without intricate fabrics or finishes. DIY cleaning cuts labor charges using affordable store-grade cleaners.

5. Compare Furniture Cleaner Estimates

Do some due diligence in requesting multiple quotes. Ensure aligned expectations on service levels so apples-to-apples pricing. Established firms with buying power often hold better product rates too.

We hope these tips help clients and homeowners budget for quality furniture cleaning services. At Shiny Carpet Cleaning, we offer customized packages to suit any style and price range — from a quick surface refresh to whole-room makeovers.

Is It Possible To Save Money On Furniture Cleaning?

Yes, there are many opportunities to make your furniture cleaning even cheaper. A few times a year, your local furniture cleaning service will have deals and specials that are almost too good to be true, and you should keep your eyes and ears open to take advantage of them.

You can also save some money by having more furniture cleaned at one time. Furniture cleaners will be happy to travel less to clean more items, so they will make the price of cleaning each item lower and you can have an entire house full of clean furniture.

You also might find a cleaner who will let you bring smaller items into their shop. If you save them the time and effort of travel, your local furniture cleaning pro might give you a better price on your furniture. You also might just ask for a discount when you talk to a furniture cleaner, you never know what they might say.
